text:
Support Ops: FYI getting a customer escalation — p99 latency spikes from ap-south1 over the last 45m. They report large TLS handshake times and a lot of cross-AZ hops. Customer says it started after a deploy earlier today. :rotating_light:

Eva: thanks, can you paste a sample trace? need to see if it's TLS or routing.

Support Ops: here's a short repro from their side (sanitized):

Support Ops: ```
curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" 
*   Trying 103.12.45.78...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to api.redwood-inference.com (103.12.45.78) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLS handshake, Server hello (2)
* TLS handshake, Certificate (11)
* TLS handshake, Server finished (14)
* TLS handshake, Client finished (16)
* SSL connection using TLSv1.3 / TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood-inference.com
> ...
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK

Request total: 1.8s  (p99 ~1.6s -> used to be ~120ms)
TLS handshake portion: ~1.4s
```

Raj: that TLS time is huge. Could be upstream handshake retries or a network hairpin. Any traceroutes?

Support Ops: yes — they ran traceroute from their client in Mumbai to api ->

Support Ops: ```
traceroute to api.redwood-inference.com (103.12.45.78), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1 (10.0.0.1)  0.6 ms  0.4 ms  0.5 ms
 2  203.0.113.12 (203.0.113.12)  8.1 ms  7.9 ms  8.2 ms
 3  * * *
 4  198.51.100.22 (198.51.100.22)  40.2 ms  42.5 ms  41.8 ms
 5  103.12.45.78 (103.12.45.78)  120.4 ms  118.9 ms  119.6 ms
```

Support Ops: looks like an extra hop or multiline routing depending on time. They also queried DNS a bunch — sometimes resolving to 103.12.45.78 (ap-south1-pop1) and sometimes to 203.0.113.55 (ap-south1-pop3) within the same TTL window.

Marta: could be DNS TTL mispropagated from our edge control plane or a geo-affinity drift. NetBot, do we have any control-plane changes around 1923450000-1923453000?

NetBot: [control-plane-audit] 1923449000: edge route rebalancer started rolling affinity adjustments for ap-south1. 1923451200: affinity delta=+0.18 applied to pop3. 1923454000: job completed.

Eva: ok that timing matches. If customers resolve to different POPs mid-session we can get TLS re-handshake to different certs/instances and increased latency due to cross-AZ pathing. We also had a canary of route-change yesterday that adjusted BGP anycast weights. That could explain intermittent resolves.

Raj: I want to confirm if these are TLS full handshakes or 0-RTT suppressed. From the curl trace it was a full handshake. Are we evicting TCP/TLS connection reuse on the LB due to source IP affinity mismatch?

SRE Oncall: checking LB logs for that IP block now. One minute.

SRE Oncall: LB logs show 503 connection drain events around 1923456000 for several sessions hitting pop1 -> pop3 handoff. Also seeing increased SYN retransmits from a small subset of ASes in IN.

Support Ops: customer says they see the problem much worse during 08:00-09:30 IST. That matches the rebalancer window.

Marta: mitigation plan: 1) pause/revert rebalancer for ap-south1, 2) add short-term DNS stickiness (override TTL to 30s), 3) enable fallback route-pin for active sessions to avoid cross-pop handoff. Thoughts?

Eva: +1 to pausing. Reverting will stop churn immediately. For DNS TTL override we need infra approval — might be fine as temporary.

Raj: also suggest we check our cert rotation boundaries — if different POPs present different cert chains (intermediate ordering) that could increase handshake size. Not likely but worth verifying.

SRE Oncall: initiating revert of rebalancer now. Rolling back to affinity state at 1923448000. Will monitor.

NetBot: [deployment] revert-edge-rebalancer-ap-south1 started by SRE Oncall at 1923457001.

Support Ops: I've told the customer we've paused the rebalancer and to expect improved p99 in 10-15m if DNS propagation cooperates. They've asked for a postmortem when we know root cause.

Eva: quick thing — can we also temporarily enable TCP keepalive and increase idle timeout on the LB for the affected pools? That would reduce full handshake frequency if clients are re-resolving.

SRE Oncall: I can flip LB idle timeout to 15m for the ap-south1 pool. Doing now.

SRE Oncall: LB timeout updated. Watching metrics.

SRE Oncall: 1923457189 — p99 for the customer's consumer key down from 1.6s -> 180ms. Looks like revert helped.

Support Ops: customer confirms improvement, still occasional spikes ~350ms when resolving to the other POP but much better overall. They asked for follow-up items.

Marta: follow-ups to include in postmortem: - root cause (rebalancer policy change + BGP weight tweak) - why DNS responses varied so much (race between zone updates + resolver caching) - why LB/connection affinity didn't protect active sessions - mitigation timeline and rollback playbook - engineer owners and timeline

Eva: action items: 1) infra to add a safety throttle to route rebalancer (limit changes per window) — owner: Raj; 2) edge team to ensure LB preserves session affinity during route shuffles — owner: SRE Oncall; 3) platform to add short-circuit config to force lower DNS TTL for rolling windows — owner: Marta; 4) run synthetic p95/p99 tests for ap-south1 during next rebalancer run — owner: Support Ops

Raj: I noted the safety throttle as a ticket: INFRA-3892. Will add checks for BGP weight deltas >0.1 to require manual approval.

Marta: I'll draft the postmortem and ping the customer with timeline + mitigation.

Support Ops: thanks all. tagging @customer-success to coordinate postmortem delivery. :thumbsup:

NetBot: [alert] edge-route-rebalancer-ap-south1 reverted; anomalies cleared (p99 reduced)

Eva: good work. We'll follow up with a more detailed RCA once we have the logs and BGP diffs.

SRE Oncall: closing thread when postmortem is published.
